paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me. No oppressor is as big as he thinks he is. The king of Babylon struck the nations "with unceasing blows," and still the LORD "has broken the staff of the wicked" (Isaiah 14:5-6). Whoever is squeezing you right now, the LORD sees it, and He isn't scared of them.

Now look at what the king said in his heart: "I will make myself like the Most High" (Isaiah 14:14). I think that's the whole problem in one line. He wanted the throne that only God has, and the song says he ended up "brought down to Sheol" instead (Isaiah 14:15). I once spent years at the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I know how the high seat looks from down there, and I'm glad the Most High is the One sitting in it.

And don't miss how the passage starts. "For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob; once again He will choose Israel and settle them in their own land" (Isaiah 14:1). The same God who brings down the proud also gives rest to the hurting (Isaiah 14:3). So you can hold on to hope today, baker, because the One in charge is on the side of His people.
